decisions.reason: As a 2023 launch that builds directly on the established offer and already received its own webpage, it carries visible commitment and strategic fit, so management would be reluctant to withdraw it so soon without clear failure evidence.

The building data digital twin service extends the firm's core geospatial integration business and fits its forward-looking direction, so despite only modest public visibility the firm is likely to continue backing it.

This authentication and identity delegation service is close to the existing offer and relevant for enterprise integration, but with less visible public commitment than some others it has a somewhat higher—still minority—chance of being dropped.
An open GIS application development framework matches the firm's open, extensible and R&D-oriented positioning, making continued support more likely than an early exit.

Because this GIS identity and access service was publicly launched as a new offering and supports the firm's push toward integrated enterprise geospatial solutions, management would tend to persist with it.
